finding.claim: Blind SSRF through webhook callback URL. Any caller of POST /subscribe can register an arbitrary callbackUrl. The server then POSTs the payload to it every minute, including to internal hosts such as 169.254.169.254, localhost, or private-network services. The response is discarded, so the SSRF is blind, but it can still reach internal endpoints with a POST and a controlled payload.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-supplied URL
URL stored in the subscriptions map with no validation (no scheme, host, or IP check)
the scheduled job iterates over all stored callback URLs
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI from the stored value
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, no host or private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking, no DNS pinning, and no auth shown on /subscribe. Only one file exists, so there is no upstream middleware to check. The default HttpClient does not follow redirects, which does not mitigate direct internal targets.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 POSTs to it via client.send. The only regex guard is in thumb() at line 30, which is a different path. Auth on /subscribe is not shown, and the single file contains no routing code.
